findings.where: First screen (desktop and phone), the nav, and the page's foot: the contact action and the pad-yellow address strip
findings.fault: There is no way to reach Mark anywhere on the page. The first screen has no action, no email address and no Contact item in the nav, and the foot of the page ends on a colophon. parts.txt lists only the home link, three nav anchors, the PDF link and the replay button, so no mailto link exists at all. The tile's own palette and texture notes describe a pad-yellow 'address strip' at the foot of the sheet, but that strip was never built.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has read Mark's line and credential and wants to engage him finds nothing to click or copy, and has to search elsewhere for his email. The founder's personal-advisor test asks for 'one direct, personal way to reach him', and the brief asks for one action with the address shown. Both fail.

findings.where: Motion sketch panel (desktop-05, phone-03 and phone-04)
findings.fault: The motion specimen sits on a large lavender field. This colour is not among the tile's four declared colours and has no role in the palette. It is the loudest ground on the page and breaks the direction's 'one soft ground, blue and grey as the only ink'.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for the house blue and grey with restraint. A lilac block reads as off-brand, and as a little 'fun', on a counsel's-paper tile for a PPP lawyer.

findings.where: Article specimen: the subheads 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' and 'Download'
findings.fault: The subheads are set in a heavy, wide black grotesque. It is a third face, outside the stated pair, which gives Newsreader 500 for subheads. Its blunt weight reads like a tech or startup display face next to the light serif.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and the founder. The article specimen is meant to show the type system she will reuse, and it shows a face the pair doesn't contain. The brief also bans anything that reads 'in-your-face techy' or not refined.

findings.where: Article specimen title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law'
findings.fault: The title is set in a heavy bold serif at very large size. The type pair names no such weight (Light 300 for the display line, 400 for reading, 500 for subheads), so the article's top heading contradicts the hero's light, refined voice. The title also uses a straight apostrophe ('World's') where the rest of the page uses curly quotes.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges whether the article page belongs to the same identity as the hero. A reader of a legal-journal-style page would also notice the typewriter apostrophe in the largest line.

findings.fault: Each swatch has a different shape and edge. The paper swatch is a square-cornered box with a grey hairline. The grey swatch is a rounded rectangle. The blue swatch is an ellipse with a dark outline. The yellow swatch has a thick blue border. Four items of one kind get four treatments, and the blue-edged yellow swatch looks like a focused or selected control.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the tile as a system. The page claims 'square at every corner' for its one frame, but its own specimen mixes radii and shapes at random, so the swatch row looks unfinished.

findings.fault: The 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' line is pushed to the far right, away from the title it describes. The row then runs straight into the lavender motion panel with no space below it, on both desktop and phone.
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning for the PDF: on desktop the date and format read as a stray label rather than part of the link. The cramped join also makes the download look like part of the motion panel.

findings.fault: This is a button, but it is styled as an underlined blue prose link. That is the look the page reserves for navigation (the PDF link has the same look), so it reads as a link that would go somewhere.
findings.who_objects: Angélique or a later builder reading the tile as the system: one look now means two functions, navigate and act.

findings.where: First screen (desktop and phone): name, credential and supporting line
findings.fault: The first screen says what Mark does and for whom, but not where. The brief's own material gives the regions of his work (Melbourne, Istanbul, São Paulo talks), yet no base country or region appears.
findings.who_objects: A development-agency officer choosing an advisor by region of experience: they can't tell from the first screen whether he works in theirs.
